turns.q:
Your response was: "Looked at it. Checkout flow. Nearly missed the submit button. It barely registered visually — took a moment to find the action I needed."

We want to understand what you meant by "nearly missed the submit button", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The "Place Order" button is positioned at the very bottom of the layout, below a large "Continue Shopping" button, pushing the primary action to the lowest point on the screen.

B) The "Place Order" button appears visually subordinate to "Continue Shopping" — it is smaller in size and sits beneath a much more prominent, full-width element, making it harder to identify as the main action.

C) There is no label or section heading near the "Place Order" button to signal that it is the final checkout action, leaving it visually unanchored from the payment form above it.

D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant (you must still name the specific element you were referring to)

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.
What kind of work situation typically brings you to review a checkout layout like this one?
turns.a: Group purchase. Deadline. I'm executing the final action on behalf of others. Primary CTA needs to be obvious — no searching required.

turns.q: When you looked at that screen on behalf of the group, what were you trying to confirm was clearly visible in the layout before you could consider the order done?
turns.a: Find and execute the primary CTA on the first scan. One look, one action. Not search and re-read to confirm it's available.

turns.q: If the "Place Order" button were redesigned to feel like the dominant action in this layout, what would that look like to you?
turns.a: 'Place Order' visible in under three seconds. Reads as active — high contrast, readable label. Execute it, confirmation appears. Zero scanning, zero re-reading to confirm it's available. That's the success state.

turns.q: When you look at the "Place Order" button in this layout, what is it about its appearance — the fill, the color, the border style — that stops it from reading as the dominant action?
turns.a: 'Place Order' has gray fill on gray background, 12px label — reads as a disabled state. Not immediately identifiable as an active button. Had to scan past it and re-read to confirm it was even available. The affordance was wrong: inactive-looking styling on the primary action.
